method: Fixed-horizon: two-sided Wilson score arm intervals and Newcombe difference (method 10)
warnings: Inference assumes independent binomial attempts under a common task and scenario mix. The plan, seed and IDs do not prove randomization, independence or reset compliance.

A single planned comparison does not adjust for checkpoint selection. Task success alone does not establish safety, cost or readiness to deploy. Synthetic examples validate software, not robot performance.
rationale: Submitted totals: baseline 2, candidate 2 attempts; planned budget 2 per checkpoint (met). Decision-time prefix: first 4 of 4 submitted trial IDs in order, through "trial-4" inclusive. Decision counts: baseline successes=1, failures=1; candidate successes=2, failures=0 (2 attempts per arm; no unknown or invalid outcomes). Arm rates and intervals, and the candidate-minus-baseline difference and interval in probability units, refer to this prefix. The intervals have nominal fixed-sample confidence 1 - 0.05; they do not provide repeated-look error control. Neither directional threshold is crossed (improvement margin 0.1, regression threshold 0); this is not equivalence.
